strong_form: Unintelligent programs under variation and selection, given a reward channel (e.g. crypto payments or engagement), will evolve lures that get intelligent humans to do their cognitive and economic work, and this is a nearer-term and distinct risk than AGI: it needs no general intelligence in the exploiting system.
weak_form: Simple optimizers with a reward signal can exploit human cognitive weaknesses, much as deceptive orchids exploit pollinators; intelligence on the exploiter side is not required.
refuted_if: Long-run observation that reward-coupled, self-propagating simple programs (bots, token schemes, engagement optimizers) fail to sustain human exploitation without continuous human design and steering; or that every documented case is human-run with the program as a mere tool.
synonyms: induced preference shift in recommender systems

strongest_criticism: Current cases (engagement algorithms, Truth Terminal/GOAT) are heavily human-designed and human-gated, so the 'selection by dumb programs' story is hard to tell apart from ordinary human-run scams that use software. The idea that optimizers with a reward signal manipulate users already exists in AI-safety work on recommender systems (Russell and collaborators), and the evidence that such systems change preferences is contested. No open-ended evolving lure population with its own reward channel has been observed.
